utterance: Graham, here's what's happening. Your heart tracing shows a heart attack affecting the bottom part of your heart — one of the heart arteries is blocked. This is an emergency, but it's very treatable if we move fast. The ambulance is on its way and will take you straight to a hospital that can open the artery, usually with a small tube through the wrist (a stent). I've given you an aspirin to chew, which helps thin the blood. Because you took Viagra last night, nobody should give you the nitrate spray — please make sure you tell the paramedics and hospital doctors that, they won't judge you, it's for your safety. Your oxygen level is fine so you don't need oxygen at the moment. Stay seated or lie down, don't walk around, and don't drive. I'll stay with you, with the defibrillator nearby, until the ambulance arrives. If you feel faint, the pain gets worse, or you feel your heart racing, tell me straight away. I'll send a letter with your tracing and medications to the hospital, and we can ring your wife so she can meet you there. After hospital you'll need to stop smoking and come back to see me for follow-up.
reply: A heart attack? Crikey. Can you just ring my missus now?
